newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rights group says Lebanon torturing Christians.
newsitem.headline: Rights group says Lebanon torturing Christians.

text.p: An international human rights watchdog accused Lebanon on Tuesday of torturing Christians seized in a wave of detentions and said its own correspondent in Beirut had been detained.

"The International Federation of Human Rights Leagues (FIDH) has learned that some of those arrested have been victims of torture, notably the method known as 'the banana' -- being hung by the arms with the hands tied behind the back," the Paris-based group said in a statement.
"The FIDH has good reason to believe that others, if not all of these (detained) persons are even now being tortured," the group added.
It said Wail Kheir, head of FIDH's Lebanese affiliated Foundation for Human and Humanitarian Rights, was being held and demanded his immediate release.

FIDH listed the names of 26 individuals it said had been detained in the past week. It said it appeared they had been arrested merely on the assumption they were members of the political opposition or sympathisers.
All were detained without arrest warrants by individuals in civilian clothing and were immediately taken to the Defence Ministry, the group said.
"The FIDH asks the Lebanese authorities to free those it has detained and to immediately stop using torture and other inhuman, cruel and degrading methods," it said.
It urged the international community to intervene with the Lebanese authorities to help end the alleged violations.

Lebanese Prosecutor-General Adnan Addoum acknowledged on Monday that 48 people had been held in a wave of detentions of opposition figures in Lebanon in the past few days but said 26 had already been freed.
None of the detainees had been charged with any offences, he told reporters in Beirut.
